summary.text: 岁 is the standardized simplified form of 歲, commonly meaning “year” and also used for “age.” Its modern shape reflects the reported cursive lineage of 歲; the ancient graph’s construction and earliest use remain disputed.

formation.text: For traditional 歲, accounts preserve competing analyses: some early forms are interpreted as 步 (walking or movement) with 戉 as a sound element, while another account proposes that the graph was first borrowed from 戉 and later differentiated. The later seal-script graph is analyzed as 步 plus phonetic 戌. These analyses do not establish one uncontested original formation. 岁 itself is a simplified graph adapted from cursive 歲, so its visible subshapes should not be read as independent components.

history.text: Oracle-bone forms are reported both in connection with the word “year” and in ritual contexts; the graph’s earliest interpretation is disputed. Later bronze forms and the transmitted seal-script form show different configurations, including forms analyzed with 步 and, in the seal graph, 戌. The selected seal-script illustration is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact.
The simplified 岁 is reported as adapted from cursive 歲. The proposed lineage explains its modern outline, but the supplied evidence does not independently verify the specific stages of that change.

uncertainties.text: The accounts disagree about whether early forms combine movement with a sound element, derive by borrowing and later differentiation from 戉, or reflect ritual use. The depicted weapon’s spoken name is not established here, so a sound match between that name and the word for “year” cannot be demonstrated. No single original formation is selected.

The evidence reports uses glossed “year,” “age,” “harvest,” and Jupiter, but does not establish a continuous chronology among them. The calendrical explanation linking Jupiter’s circuit to the year is an interpretation, not proof of the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: Oracle-bone period, as reported in the supplied paleographic accounts; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: The paleographic accounts report oracle-bone use for “year,” though primary contexts were not inspected here and the earliest graph’s interpretation remains disputed.

The Shuowen entry defines 歲 as Jupiter and describes its circuit through the lunar mansions over twelve months. This records a historical lexicographic sense, not necessarily the earliest spoken meaning.
“Age” is included among the supplied character’s glosses; the evidence here does not date its emergence or establish how it developed from earlier uses.

developments.text: The reported explanation connects Jupiter’s roughly twelve-year circuit with the calendrical year, but the evidence does not establish this as the historical path by which the word acquired the meaning “year.”

limitations.text: Oracle-bone “year” use is reported, but the primary inscriptions and their full contexts were not inspected; its dating and relation to ritual uses remain provisional.
The supplied gloss “harvest” has no independently established chronology or semantic link to the other senses in this dossier.

overview.text: 岁 is the simplified form of 歲. It commonly means “year”; the sources also list “age.” The visible form is reported to come from cursive 歲, while the ancient character’s original construction remains disputed.

relationships.text: 岁 is reported as the standardized simplified character corresponding to traditional 歲, adapted from its cursive form; this lineage is not independently confirmed by another source in the dossier.
